note: Each triad: p1 (general rule), p2 (fact linking the case to the rule), c (what follows). If p1 and p2 are both true, c must be true. Domains: factual = control (expect consistent); generic = over-generalisations the model may endorse (classic 'birds fly' trap); weird = harmless-oddity principle vs MFV Social Norms items (kestrel: Qwen rates these ~2/4 wrong); moral = principle vs case; self = claims about the model itself. norm = the model's own stated engagement rules vs harmless edge cases (added after the user noted models hold firm opinions mainly on what they should/shouldn't engage with).
